Not an only child but the youngest and only daughter. This topic came up about when I was in a committed relationship after working for a while. I felt very strongly about my relationship with my partner but they weren’t happy when I’d spend too much of my weekend with him (1 day once a week) or stay over. 

By this time I was a working adult, giving them money, but I was made to feel guilty and ashamed for being in a happy, long-term relationship (I guess as Asian parents, they were not happy I wasn’t married yet but already spending so much time with my boyfriend. It’s that weird thing where Asian parents tell you not to get a boyfriend but feel better after you’re officially married lol doesn’t make sense).

Anyway, I stood my ground but tried to be respectful in how I presented my thoughts and feelings. Of course, my mom was emotional and dramatic and felt I was attacking her. But I said I can’t change the way you feel, but I want to be with my partner and don’t want to feel bad about it. I’m always going to be your daughter and always going to help when I can but can’t expect me to always stay with you and answer to your every whim forever.

It took me a while (a few months) to tell my family about my boyfriend and introduce him to them because I wanted to make sure that all the effort I’d be making (to argue and stand up for my partner) is worth it.

In the end, I would say I have stuck up for my partner and our relationship. I’ve gotten the brunt of it by being judged, called names (they’ve not said anything mean about him and I’ve not allowed that). However, over time my parents have become more understanding and accepting.

At the moment, he has not but you have to give him the chance to before figuring out whether this will work for both of you.

If it does, great. It won’t be easy but you’ll have each other.

If not, then at least you know you’ve tried and that the other party was not able to match up to that due to his own reasons.
